QF.id: AIFM Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_17

question.text: On the graph of Capital Market Theory, the Capital Market Line (CML) is drawn as the tangent from the risk-free rate to the efficient frontier of risky assets. The point of tangency is called the Market Portfolio (M). Which of the following statements about the Market Portfolio is INCORRECT?

answer.text: The Market Portfolio theoretically contains all risky assets — domestic and foreign stocks, bonds, real estate, commodities, and so on.
In practice, a broad-based equity index is used as a proxy for the Market Portfolio.
The Market Portfolio has only systematic risk because all unsystematic risk has been diversified away.
The correlation between the return on the Market Portfolio and the return on the risk-free asset is +1, since both lie on the CML.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 5.3 / Box 5.1: the risk-free asset has zero correlation with every risky asset, including the market portfolio. Its standard deviation is zero, so correlation is undefined/zero. All other three statements are correct definitions. The Trap: Candidates see the CML as a straight line and incorrectly infer 'correlation +1'. Lying on the same line does not imply perfect correlation — the risk-free asset has zero variance. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C workbook chapter sample Q2 and Q3. XXI-B tests 'completely diversified portfolio correlates +1 with market portfolio'. Manager's Pro-Tip: When an LP challenges your AIF's benchmark as an 'imperfect market proxy' (e.g., Nifty 500), concede — the workbook itself acknowledges there is 'no unanimity' on proxy choice. Offer a custom composite benchmark in the side letter.
